history.summary: The Bansiwala (Banshi Wale Ka) Mandir stands near the Brahamani Mata Mandir at Kathariyon/Kathadiyon Ka Chowk, Bhandariyon Ki Gali, Nagaur city, about 3 km from the Nagaur bus stand. IGNCA/ASI documentation (RJ/NGR-052) dates it to the 16th century AD. It is a single-storey stone temple, east-facing, with a carved torana (arched gateway) and elaborately carved door panels with foliage motifs; the sanctum is a small closed chamber housing the deity's shrine under a silver chhatri, with a glittering glass-and-mirror interior and painted tiles. Visitor reviews note a large spacious hall, a Krishna shrine and a Shiv garbh griha. The temple is in active religious use, well maintained, and assessed in fair condition. The IGNCA record's own coordinates (27°40'N, 75°15'E) are coarse; the listed latitude/longitude are from geocoding the temple's Nagaur address.

town_description: Nagaur is a historic town in central Rajasthan, once the capital of the Jangladesh region and ruled by the Nagaur Chauhan Rajputs. It is known for Nagaur Fort (Ahhichatragarh), the Tarkeen Dargah, traditional havelis, and the annual Nagaur Cattle Fair, one of Asia's largest livestock fairs. The town is on the Jodhpur-Bikaner rail line.
